title: Timeline tracks reorder by dragging their headers, the same physical way layer rows do
goal: The user asked (2026-09-30) for the lifting, make-room drag to work on the timeline track headers too. Tracks cannot be reordered at all today, so a person who wants a title track above the recording has no way to move it. Dragging a track header should lift it, the other tracks slide aside, and it lands in the gap.
notes: Split off dragging-a-layer-feels-physical-the-row-lifts-ri, which built the layers-list half: PhotonzCore/LayerRowDrag.swift (halves, gap, offsets, spring-open, tested) and Photonz/LayerRowDragSession.swift + LayerRowDragViews.swift (lifted row, gap, edge autoscroll through the AppKit scroll view, Escape via a local key monitor, allowsWindowActivationEvents for click-through). The same model should drive track headers: tracks are rows of one pitch. grep found no track reorder anywhere today (EditorState+Tracks.swift, TimelineTrackRows.swift).
acceptance: Pressing a track header and moving lifts the whole track (header and lane) under the pointer, locked horizontally
The other tracks spring out of the way and the gap they open is where the track lands; letting go settles it there in one undo step, Escape puts it back
Track order and the layers list stay the same story: reordering tracks reorders the layers they hold, and the layers list shows it
A walk at Next defaults drags a track by the pointer and photographs it mid-drag and after

Pre-build review: (1) tracks have different heights (sound lanes taller, key/zoom lanes under clips, group headings), so the layer model's fixed pitch cannot be reused: a new TrackRowDrag reads halves of variable-height rows, same rule as the layers list. (2) Groups: above/below a grouped track joins its group, bottom half of an open heading is the group's first slot, top half of the row under a group lands below it; folded heading's bottom half is below the whole group. (3) Found by reading: a clip's own sound picks the first audio track it fits, so swapping two audio tracks would swap the headers but leave the waveforms where they were; pinning the clip's sound to its track when tracks are written down (test reproduces it first). (4) Locked tracks do not lift, like locked layers. (5) Premiere does not let you drag tracks at all; this goes beyond it. Gated on the same Next switch as the layer lift (on at Next defaults).
